name: Guardian genius crossword No 222
preamble: Each down clue contains a superfluous word to be ignored in producing the solution to be entered in the grid. Each across entry in the grid may be deduced from its clue, combined in the same way with one of the superfluous down clue words.

solutions.check: grid and clues read from the Guardian's printable PDF, its numbering matching the clue list; each light's entry one fifteensquared prints for it, the only choice of them whose crossings all agree; an entry not its answer carries the answer as its alteration's `from`

clue.text: Swimming coach at university produces means of enhancing breath

indicators.note: when your head is swimming everything is jumbled, so the word beside it comes out in a muddled order

blocks.note: taken as written
U is the standard abbreviation for university

explanation.surface: A swimming coach working at a university is selling breath mints on the side.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue solves to CACHOU, a scented sweet for the breath; the grid takes its sound-alike CASHEW, which the spare word 'nut' in 1 Down defines.
explanation.definitionFit: A cachou is a small scented lozenge sucked to sweeten the breath.

clue.text: Shelled pecan nut oddly contains second husk

indicators.note: a shelled nut has lost its outside, so the word loses its first and last letters
done oddly means done in a strange way, so the remaining letters are rearranged
one part holds the other inside it, like a box holding its contents

blocks.note: the pecan without its first and last letters
S is the abbreviation for second
the spare word, ignored here; it defines 1 Across, CASHEW

explanation.surface: Shelling pecans, someone finds a strange seed inside the husk.
explanation.walkthrough: With 'nut' set aside, the inner letters of pecan are rearranged to CAE, and S goes inside to make CASE.
explanation.definitionFit: A case is the outer covering of a seed or fruit, the same thing as its husk or shell.

clue.text: Cold nurse disregards injured dog

indicators.note: something injured is knocked out of shape, so the letters of the words before it are bent into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
the spare word, ignored here; it defines 24 Across, OVERSEES, in its old sense of overlook or neglect

explanation.surface: An unfeeling nurse ignores a hurt dog.
explanation.walkthrough: With 'disregards' set aside, the clue is an anagram of COLD NURSE.
explanation.definitionFit: Dog is an old insult for a contemptible man, a villain or rogue.

clue.text: Superfluous meeting for person with an insignificant role

blocks.note: first meaning: more than is needed, surplus
second meaning: a film actor in a crowd scene
the spare word, ignored here; it defines 21 Across, SESSION

explanation.surface: Someone with a tiny part in proceedings sits through a pointless meeting.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue's first word sounds like a nod to the puzzle's own spare words, but here it is a plain definition; the spare word is 'meeting'.
explanation.definitionFit: Extra means additional or surplus, and as a noun it names a film performer hired for a non-speaking background part.

clue.text: Cunning trick with edges of special cube

indicators.note: the edges of a word are its outermost letters, first and last

blocks.note: the first and last letters of special
eight is the cube of two

explanation.surface: A conjuror pulls off a sly trick using the edges of a specially made die.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue solves to SLEIGHT; the grid takes its sound-alike SLIGHT, which the spare word 'insult' in 25 Down defines.
explanation.definitionFit: Sleight is skilful deception, as in sleight of hand, the conjuror's art of trickery.

clue.text: Lesson for artist in story about girl stealing fine piece

indicators.note: whatever is stolen is taken in and held, so one letter goes inside the word for story

blocks.note: a story is a fib or lie
F is the abbreviation for fine, as on pencil leads
C is short for circa, Latin for about
a lass is a girl
the spare word, ignored here; it defines 17 Across, DRAUGHT, a piece in the board game

explanation.surface: An art lesson features in a tale about a girl who steals a fine painting.
explanation.walkthrough: With 'piece' set aside, note that in the surface the girl does the stealing, but in the wordplay it is the story that takes in the fine.
explanation.definitionFit: A life class is an art class where students draw or paint from a live model.

clue.text: Women thrown out of mature rock band

indicators.note: something thrown out is expelled, so a letter leaves the word that follows

blocks.note: W is the abbreviation for women, the letter removed
to mature is to grow up
the spare word, ignored here; it defines 29 Across, GNEISS

explanation.surface: Women are ejected from an ageing rock band.
explanation.walkthrough: With 'rock' set aside, W comes out of GROW UP. 'Rock band' reads as one phrase, but rock is the spare word and band alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A group is a band of musicians who play together.

clue.text: Soldiers backing up corruption can lead to general persecuting hanger-on

indicators.note: in a down clue going up means reading from the bottom, so the word for corruption runs in reverse
the lead of a word is its first letter, the one at the front

blocks.note: rot is decay or corruption
men are soldiers, as opposed to officers
a tin is a can
the first letter of general
the spare word, ignored here; it defines 28 Across, LEECH

explanation.surface: Troops supporting a corrupt regime may lead a general to harass his followers.
explanation.walkthrough: With 'hanger-on' set aside, the soldiers are the ordinary ranks, not officers, and 'can' is the noun for a metal container, not the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To torment is to persecute, inflicting lasting suffering or distress on someone.

clue.text: Enlist beauty wanting to learn actors' lines

indicators.note: wanting means lacking, so the word for enlist goes without the letters for learn

blocks.note: to conscript is to enlist compulsorily
to con is an old word for to learn or study, the letters removed
the spare word, ignored here; it defines 22 Across, BELLE

explanation.surface: Someone wants to sign up a beautiful actress who does not care to learn her lines.
explanation.walkthrough: With 'beauty' set aside, CON is taken from the front of CONSCRIPT. To con, meaning to study or memorise, is an old word.
explanation.definitionFit: A script is the written text of a play or film, holding the words the actors speak.

clue.text: Held forth regularly about red alert going off

indicators.note: regularly means at even intervals, so every other letter is kept
something going off has exploded, so these letters fly apart and land in a new order

blocks.note: the first, third and fifth letters of about
taken as written
the spare word, ignored here; it defines 30 Across, TOCSIN, an alarm bell

explanation.surface: Someone kept lecturing about the red alert as the alarm sounded.
explanation.walkthrough: With 'alert' set aside, alternate letters of about join RED and the six letters are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: To orate is to deliver a speech in a grand way, which is what holding forth means.

clue.text: Hi-tech utensil contains means of waste disposal

indicators.note: the words before it hold the answer inside them, spread across the gap between them

blocks.note: found running from the end of the first word into the second

explanation.surface: A gadget-laden kitchen tool includes a built-in rubbish disposal.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue solves to CHUTE; the grid takes its sound-alike SHOOT, which the spare word 'photograph' in 18 Down defines.
explanation.definitionFit: A rubbish chute is a sloping channel that carries refuse down from upper floors to bins below.

clue.text: Go round bend, taking issue with occupier of bed

indicators.note: taking something in means holding it, so one word sits inside the other

blocks.note: to corner is to go round a bend, as a car does
to issue is to flow out

explanation.surface: A driver takes a bend while arguing with whoever is sleeping in the bed.
explanation.walkthrough: The bed is a flower bed, not one for sleeping. The clue solves to CORNFLOWER; the grid takes its sound-alike CORNFLOUR, which the spare word 'starch' in 26 Down defines.
explanation.definitionFit: A cornflower is a blue garden plant, so it is something that grows in, or occupies, a flower bed.

clue.text: Shrink and cut growth having lost hundreds

indicators.note: what is lost is no longer there, so the named letters drop out of the words before

blocks.note: a cut is a man-made waterway, a canal
a cyst is a growth in the body
C is the Roman numeral for a hundred; both are lost

explanation.surface: A therapist prescribes shrinking and removing a growth after losing hundreds of pounds.
explanation.walkthrough: Shrink is slang for a psychiatrist. The clue solves to ANALYST; the grid takes its sound-alike ANNALIST, which the spare word 'chronicler' in 14 Down defines.
explanation.definitionFit: Shrink is informal slang for a psychiatrist, and an analyst is a psychoanalyst who treats patients.

clue.text: Officers primarily providing input to Crown Prosecution Service

definitions.text: Officers primarily providing input to Crown Prosecution Service

indicators.note: primarily means first of all, so only the opening letter is kept
input is something fed in, so one letter goes into the abbreviation

blocks.note: CPS is the abbreviation for the Crown Prosecution Service, which brings criminal cases in England
the first letter of officers

explanation.surface: Police officers mostly supply the evidence that goes to the prosecutors.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both definition and wordplay, since police supply most cases to the prosecutors. It solves to COPS; the grid takes its sound-alike COPSE, which the spare word 'Wood' in 23 Down defines.
explanation.definitionFit: Cops is informal slang for police officers, who feed criminal cases to the prosecuting authority.

clue.text: Plagiarise book to stop shy chronicler writing badly

indicators.note: a stopper plugs a gap, so these letters go into the middle of the word for shy

blocks.note: to shy is to throw or sling
to crib is to copy someone else's work
B is the abbreviation for book
the spare word, ignored here; it defines 12 Across, ANNALIST

explanation.surface: A timid historian copies a book and writes it up badly.
explanation.walkthrough: With 'chronicler' set aside, CRIB and B plug the gap in S-LING. Shy reads as an adjective but is the verb to throw.
explanation.definitionFit: Scribbling is writing hastily and carelessly so the result is messy or illegible.

clue.text: Running dog let out

blocks.note: a cur is a mongrel dog
to rent is to let out a property

explanation.surface: A dog lets itself out and goes for a run.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue solves to CURRENT; the grid takes its sound-alike CURRANT, which the spare word 'Fruit' in 21 Down defines.
explanation.definitionFit: Current means in progress now, as a running total or the running account is the current one.

clue.text: Certifies account reviled councillor corrects

blocks.note: AC is the abbreviation for account
Cr is the abbreviation for councillor
to edit is to correct a text
the spare word, ignored here; it defines 27 Across, INVEIGHED

explanation.surface: Someone vouches for an account that a much-hated councillor has been correcting.
explanation.walkthrough: With 'reviled' set aside, the clue is a straight run of AC, CR and EDITS.
explanation.definitionFit: To accredit someone is to recognise officially that they meet a standard, which is to certify them.

clue.text: Doctor behind selection of people

blocks.note: Dr is the abbreviation for doctor
aft means behind, at the back of a ship

explanation.surface: A doctor is lagging behind a group chosen from the population.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue solves to DRAFT; the grid takes its sound-alike DRAUGHT, which the spare word 'piece' in 5 Down defines, a draught being a counter in the board game draughts (checkers).
explanation.definitionFit: A draft is a group picked out for a purpose, such as soldiers chosen for service or players chosen by teams.

clue.text: Totally candid Italian photograph and Spanish articles surrounded by speculation

indicators.note: something surrounded is enclosed on all sides, so these letters sit inside the word for speculation

blocks.note: a guess is a speculation
il is the Italian for the
el is the Spanish for the, so the two words together are the Italian and Spanish articles
the spare word, ignored here; it defines 10 Across, SHOOT

explanation.surface: A frank Italian snaps photographs of Spanish goods amid wild speculation.
explanation.walkthrough: With 'photograph' set aside, 'Italian and Spanish articles' means one definite article from each language, both placed inside the speculation word after its second letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Guileless means without any cunning or deceit, so completely open and frank.

clue.text: Bring about joy unconfined

indicators.note: with no confines the word loses its boundaries, its first and last letters

blocks.note: felicity is great happiness or joy

explanation.surface: A call to set happiness free.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue solves to ELICIT; the grid takes its sound-alike ILLICIT, which the spare word 'unlicensed' in 20 Down defines.
explanation.definitionFit: To elicit a response is to draw it out or provoke it, which brings it about.

clue.text: Prize essay about unlicensed power inspired by O. Henry

indicators.note: about means around, so the word for essay wraps round what follows
to be inspired is to be breathed in, so one letter is taken in by the pair after it

blocks.note: to essay is to try or attempt
the initial O taken as written
P is the symbol for power
H is the symbol for the henry, the unit of inductance
the spare word, ignored here; it defines 19 Across, ILLICIT

explanation.surface: A prize-winning essay on bootleg electricity drew inspiration from the short-story writer O. Henry.
explanation.walkthrough: With 'unlicensed' set aside, P sits inside O and H, and TRY goes round all three. O. Henry the writer is split into O and the henry unit.
explanation.definitionFit: A trophy is a cup or other object awarded as a prize for winning.

clue.text: Surrender item that’s charged after tax

indicators.note: after places the word it follows second, so the charged item comes behind the tax

blocks.note: cess is an old word for a tax or levy
an ion is an electrically charged particle

explanation.surface: Someone gives up an item that was billed on top of tax.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Charged' suggests a price, but here it means electrically charged. The clue solves to CESSION; the grid takes its sound-alike SESSION, which the spare word 'meeting' in 3 Down defines.
explanation.definitionFit: Cession is the formal giving up of rights or territory to another, a ceding or surrender.

clue.text: Fruit flies originally propagated in bits of fruit

indicators.note: originally means at the start, so the first letter is kept
the first letter goes inside the word that follows

blocks.note: seeds are small parts of a fruit
the first letter of propagated
the spare word, ignored here; it defines 15 Across, CURRANT

explanation.surface: Fruit flies breed in pieces of fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: With 'Fruit' set aside, flies stops being part of fruit flies and becomes the verb. P goes into SEEDS after the S.
explanation.definitionFit: To speed is to move very fast, and flies is used the same way, as in time flies.

clue.text: Person who made telephone call

blocks.note: first meaning: Alexander Graham Bell, credited with inventing the telephone
second meaning: in British slang, to give someone a ring on the phone

explanation.surface: Someone made a phone call.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain 'give me a bell' means phone me. The clue solves to BELL; the grid takes its sound-alike BELLE, which the spare word 'beauty' in 8 Down defines.
explanation.definitionFit: Alexander Graham Bell patented the telephone, and a bell is informal British slang for a phone call.

clue.text: Wood shelter protects east entrance to Victoria Embankment

indicators.note: to protect is to shield all round, so the shelter word goes round the letters after it
the entrance is the way in, so the first letter is taken

blocks.note: the lee is the sheltered side, away from the wind
E is the abbreviation for east
the first letter of Victoria
the spare word, ignored here; it defines 13 Across, COPSE

explanation.surface: A wooden shelter guards the east gate onto London's Victoria Embankment, a road along the Thames.
explanation.walkthrough: With 'Wood' set aside, E and V go inside LEE after its L. The Victoria Embankment looks like one name, but Victoria only supplies its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A levee is a raised bank built along a river to stop flooding, an embankment.

clue.text: Start to obey passage from Bible when abroad

indicators.note: the start of a word is its first letter

blocks.note: the first letter of obey
a verse is a numbered passage of scripture
as means when, as in 'as I left'

explanation.surface: Begin obeying scripture when you are away from home.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue solves to OVERSEAS; the grid takes its sound-alike OVERSEES, which the spare word 'disregards' in 2 Down defines, using the old sense of oversee as overlook.
explanation.definitionFit: Overseas means in or to a foreign country across the sea, so abroad.

clue.text: Awful insult also guards against barrage of criticism

indicators.note: something awful is a mess, so the letters it governs are put in a new order
a guard stands round what it keeps, so one word holds the other

blocks.note: taken as written
v is short for versus, Latin for against
the spare word, ignored here; it defines 4 Across, SLIGHT

explanation.surface: A dreadful insult also protects against a torrent of criticism.
explanation.walkthrough: With 'insult' set aside, ALSO holds V, and the result is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A salvo is a burst of gunfire, and figuratively a sudden outburst of attacks or criticism.

clue.text: Wrong starch collars start to hurt lower part of member's face

indicators.note: a collar goes around a neck, so one word wraps round a letter
the start of a word is its first letter

blocks.note: a sin is a wrong
the first letter of hurt
the spare word, ignored here; it defines 11 Across, CORNFLOUR

explanation.surface: A wrongly starched collar chafes the lower part of an MP's face.
explanation.walkthrough: With 'starch' set aside, the member is a limb, not an MP, and the shin is the front face of its lower part.
explanation.definitionFit: The shin is the front surface of the leg below the knee, the lower part of a limb.

clue.text: Attack fantastic idea out of envy reportedly

indicators.note: what is reported is heard, so the word before it is turned into letters by sound
something fantastic is wildly imagined, so the letters are reworked into a new arrangement

blocks.note: taken as written
said aloud the two letters N and V make this word

explanation.surface: An attack arises from a crazy idea born of jealousy, so they say.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue solves to INVADE; the grid takes its sound-alike INVEIGHED, which the spare word 'reviled' in 16 Down defines.
explanation.definitionFit: To invade is to enter another country with armed force, an act of attack.

clue.text: Filter out part of notable achievement

indicators.note: the answer is only a part of the words that follow, lying inside them

blocks.note: found spanning the end of the first word and the start of the second

explanation.surface: Weed out some of a celebrated feat.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue solves to LEACH; the grid takes its sound-alike LEECH, which the spare word 'hanger-on' in 7 Down defines.
explanation.definitionFit: To leach is to drain soluble matter out of soil or rock by percolating water through it, a kind of filtering.

clue.text: Opening of nature reserve done with great care

indicators.note: the opening of a word is its first letter

blocks.note: the first letter of nature
ice is coldness of manner, a reserve

explanation.surface: Opening a nature reserve is done with great care.
explanation.walkthrough: Reserve looks like part of nature reserve, but it means aloofness. The clue solves to NICE; the grid takes its sound-alike GNEISS, which the spare word 'rock' in 6 Down defines.
explanation.definitionFit: Nice in its older sense means precise, exact or subtle, as in a nice distinction drawn with care.

clue.text: Veto books over harmful material

indicators.note: something turned over is upside down, so the letters before it run backwards

blocks.note: to nix is to veto
OT is the Old Testament, the first books of the Bible

explanation.surface: A censor bans books for containing harmful content.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue solves to TOXIN; the grid takes its sound-alike TOCSIN, an alarm bell, which the spare word 'alert' in 9 Down defines.
explanation.definitionFit: A toxin is a poison, a substance that damages living tissue.
